subject: Banking
title: Financial System Stability
description: A quick, practical guide to Financial System Stability.

hook.text: In March 2020, financial markets froze. The Fed stepped in within days, lending $2 trillion to keep the system alive.

buildup.text: Central banks monitor systemic risk. They watch for signs that a failing bank or market could trigger wider collapse.

discovery.text: Stress tests simulate crises before they happen. Banks must prove they can survive a severe recession to keep operating.

twist.text: Markets expect central bank rescues. The 'Fed put' encourages risk-taking because traders assume a safety net exists.

climax.text: Stability is the central bank's unwritten mandate. Markets function only because everyone believes the backstop exists.

punchline.text: $2 trillion in days. Central banks keep the financial system breathing.

quiz.question: What is the 'Fed put'?
options: The market expectation that the Fed will rescue markets in a crisis
